fact: The MESPTN, with KfW financing, tendered technical assistance for a pilot of the PDiMa project to digitalise civil registration services in sixteen communes, including supervision of the civil registration information system deployment, before national roll-out.

The territorial administration ministry delivered computers and printers on 8 April 2026 to five pilot communes (Golfe 1, Agoe-Nyive 1, Lacs 1, Ave 2, Zio 2) in the pilot of digitalised civil-status services, ahead of national extension.

The government officially launched on 19 December 2025 a digitalised service for civil-status acts, a pilot in five communes (Golfe 1, Agoe-Nyive 1, Ave 2, Lacs 1, Zio 2) for progressive national deployment, run by the territorial administration ministry and MESPTN through Agence Togo Digital.

Togo First reports an online system on the Services Publics platform for requesting copies of birth, marriage and death certificates, piloted in five municipalities, with the ministers committed to extending it nationwide.
source_slug: 2025-12-17 Togo Expands Public Service Digitisation With Online Civil Registry Platform

fact: Togo First reports that since December 2025 residents of five pilot municipalities can request birth, marriage and death certificate copies online through the national Services Publics platform, and Golfe 3 integrated its civil registration services into the portal in February 2025.
